description: REGRESSION WALL for saga #811, flipped by issue #815 from the characterization issue #816 built against the broken build. It asserts the CORRECT behaviour now: the check before execution runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 over the whole program and, on an `error`-severity finding, **Phase 2 never begins** — "no instruction executes, no trace event is emitted" (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`). So the `events` array is EMPTY, and that emptiness is the assertion: before the fix this program ran, produced events, and reported nothing, which is the silent wrong answer the saga is named for. Reverting the gate turns this red. Fault shape A — an UNRESOLVABLE NAME in argument position. `check()` always computed the right answer (`ol-unknown-command`, whose usual stage is `semantic` per spec/error-model.md:97); what #815 changed is that `execute()` now consults it, so the fault reaches the learner instead of the statement being discarded whole. Form under test: `when <unresolvable> [ … ]` — the handler is never registered, and the run is now refused rather than emitting an `instruction` marker and stopping. Its shape-B twin under `command-in-value-position/` produced the SAME silent stream from a DIFFERENT fault; both are now diagnosed, by different rules.
